messages:
ash: quick follow-up re: adapter surface. i want to move most route-compat & region-fallback scoring out of the policy kernel and into adapters. open to pushback.

maria: what's the core driver? testing / perf / maintainability?

ash: all three. kernel has become a grab-bag of light checks that complicate unit tests and the compile-time model. adapters already know platform constraints (region, rack, tenant flags) so they can short-circuit bad routes and tag reasons.

leo: worried about divergent behavior if adapters implement their own rules. we should define a small canonical compat spec.

ash: proposal: CompatSpec (versioned JSON-schema) + lightweight shared validators. adapters own plumbing and telemetry emission. kernel trusts validated routes and does only defensive asserts.

sophie: +1 for observability. adapters can emit which rule caused a rejection for troubleshooting. kernel should still assert on malformed route objects though.

ash: agreed. failure semantics: adapter mistake -> route filtered earlier + rich telemetry; kernel mistake -> assert/fallback to safe-pool. we also plan a "hybrid" compat_mode for rollout that emits metrics but doesn't block.

maria: suggest percent rollout flag to avoid canary surprises. how about compat_mode: adapter|kernel|hybrid with % rollout support?

ash: exact plan: default hybrid in staging. config example: { "compat_mode": "hybrid", "compat_spec_version": "2026-03-01", "telemetry_tags": ["adapter_v2"] }

leo: telemetry: add compact fingerprint label for quick queries, e.g. compat:adapter:reason=region-excluded. keeps dashboards fast.

sophie: adapters are implemented in go/rust/python. shared validator needs bindings or we offer an HTTP validator service.

maria: http validator centralizes rules but adds latency. rough numbers: local lib median 0.2ms, remote median 0.6ms, 99p up to 1.5ms cold. piggybacking on existing placement RPC could help.

ash: compromise: ship canonical local libs (go/rust) for perf; offer optional remote validator for central governance. remote mode is opt-in and rate-limited.

leo: i'll add a CI compatibility matrix exercising adapter+kernel with hybrid flag across tenants/regions. need tests to fail if spec mismatch.

ash: telemetry schema proposal: event type adapter.compat.v1 with fields adapter, tenant_id_hash, reason, outcome, spec_version, latency_ms. example: { "adapter": "kube-sidecar", "tenant_id_hash": "h:abcd", "reason": "region-block", "outcome": "rejected", "spec_version": "2026-03-01", "latency_ms": "0.4" }

ash: infra-bot pinged for retention/cost guidance on tenant_id_hash.

infra-bot: tenant_id_hash ok if hashed + sampled. recommend default 30d retention, index adapter+reason+outcome only. sample full traces at 1%.

maria: good. last ops question: does earlier adapter rejection change SLAs? it improves reliability by fast-failing, but adapter bugs could increase errors.

ash: fallback plan: monitor compat.adapter.reject_rate; if spike above threshold auto-switch impacted tenants to kernel-enforce for 5 minutes. that gives time to rollback or patch adapters.

leo: sounds actionable. i'll start the RFC PR with CompatSpec draft, telemetry schema, CI matrix. tagging sophie for telemetry review and maria for rollout ops.

sophie: i'll add Grafana panels and spike alerts for adapter.compat.v1 and the reject_rate.

ash: plan to flip staging adapters to hybrid next week if no objections. thanks all. :shipit:
